items.question: What is a basic event in reproduction?
options: Making a copy of the cell wall only
Making a copy of the DNA

items.question: When a cell copies its DNA, what else must be made before the cell divides?
options: An additional set of cellular apparatus
items.explanation: A DNA copy pushed out alone could not keep life going, so the cell also makes extra apparatus.

items.question: Bacteria live in temperate water that is warmed by global warming. Which bacteria are likely to survive?

items.question: Which disease is caused by Leishmania?

items.question: Which of these organisms reproduces by multiple fission?

items.question: Which organisms can be cut into pieces, with each piece growing into a complete organism?

items.question: Why is regeneration not the same as reproduction?
options: Most organisms do not normally depend on being cut up in order to reproduce
items.explanation: Regeneration rebuilds an organism from pieces, but reproduction does not normally rely on being broken up.

items.question: Which single-celled organism puts out small buds that separate and grow?
items.explanation: Yeast reproduces by budding, as seen in the sugar-solution activity.

items.question: In vegetative propagation, which plant parts can grow into new plants?
items.explanation: Under the right conditions, roots, stems and leaves of many plants can produce new plants.

items.question: What is one advantage of plants produced by vegetative propagation?
options: They can only grow in water
They are similar enough to the parent to have all its characteristics
items.explanation: Because they come from one parent, the new plants keep its features.

items.question: What kind of conditions does tissue culture allow plants to be grown in?

items.question: What are the thread-like structures of bread mould called?
items.explanation: The threads are hyphae; they are not the reproductive parts.

items.question: What does each Rhizopus spore eventually develop into?

items.question: When can a Rhizopus spore begin to grow?
options: When it comes into contact with a moist surface

items.question: If germ-cells with the full amount of DNA simply combined, what problem would arise?
options: Each new generation would have twice the DNA of the one before
items.explanation: Doubling the DNA every generation would upset the control of the cell; meiosis prevents this.

items.question: What is the motile germ-cell called?
items.explanation: By convention, the smaller, moving germ-cell is the male gamete.

items.question: Why is the female gamete usually the larger germ-cell?
items.explanation: The zygote needs stored energy to develop, so one gamete carries food and the other is small and motile.

items.question: What are the three parts of the pistil?
items.explanation: The swollen base is the ovary, the stalk is the style and the sticky tip is the stigma.

items.question: What is the difference between self-pollination and cross-pollination?
options: In self-pollination pollen moves within the same flower; in cross-pollination it moves to another flower
Self-pollination needs animals; cross-pollination never does
Self-pollination happens in the ovary; cross-pollination in the stigma

items.question: Which of these flowers is unisexual?
options: A flower with both stamens and pistil

items.question: Which glands add secretions to the sperms along the vas deferens?

items.question: Where does fertilisation take place in the human female?

items.question: Which change at puberty happens in both boys and girls?

items.question: How long does menstruation usually last?

items.question: Why does the lining of the uterus thicken every month?
options: To be ready to nourish an embryo if fertilisation happens
items.explanation: The uterus prepares each month in case a fertilised egg arrives.

items.question: How often does an ovary release an egg?

items.question: Which sexually transmitted infections are caused by bacteria?

items.question: Which surgical method prevents the transfer of sperms in males?

items.question: Why has prenatal sex determination been prohibited by law?
